title: Sales Enablement Playbook: Positioning, Messaging, Competitive Briefs, Pricing, Case Studies, and Security FAQ
author: Evelyn Park
content:
Overview:

This playbook consolidates Redwood Inference positioning and messaging, short competitive briefs, an AE pitch-deck outline, pricing guidance and examples, two short case studies, and a security FAQ tailored for prospects evaluating inference platforms. Use this document as the canonical go-to-market reference for demos, discovery calls, and RFP responses.

Goal:
- Help AEs and solutions engineers quickly articulate Redwood’s value for engineering and platform buyers.
- Provide concrete differentiators versus competitors, rebuttals to common objections, and reproducible pricing examples.
- Arm security conversations with precise answers and links to artifacts for further review.

Target personas and one-line value props:
1) Product / Feature Engineer (AI-native startup): "Ship LLM features faster with consistent latency and predictable unit cost."
2) Platform / Infra Team (mid-market/enterprise): "Standardize inference across teams with dedicated capacity and SLAs while keeping unit economics under control."
3) ML Engineer / MLOps: "Optimize throughput and cost with a production-ready runtime that supports quantization, KV caching, and automated batching."

Messaging pillars (3 core pillars and sample lines):
1) Production-first economics
   - Messaging: "Reduce per-token cost without sacrificing latency through intelligent batching, caching, and quantization profiles."
   - Proof points: Benchmarks show up to 3x throughput improvement on common chat workloads; sample customer reduced unit cost 40%.
2) Unified deployment model
   - Messaging: "Same API, same operational tooling across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments — simplifies rollout and governance."
   - Proof points: Private deployments include KMS integrations, audit logs, and VPC peering templates.
3) Reliability and graceful degradation
   - Messaging: "Automatic model fallbacks and routing policies keep your app online when capacity or regional disruptions occur."
   - Proof points: Built-in routing policies, canary rollouts, and configurable fallback models.

Competitive brief (one-page summary for AE):
- Competitor: MajorCloudAI (large cloud vendor)
  - Strengths: Broad cloud services, integrated data services, enterprise procurement familiarity.
  - Redwood Differentiator: Higher-performing inference runtime specialized for LLMs (KV cache, kernel selection), per-token cost visibility, and flexible private deployments with minimal infra lift.
- Competitor: SelfHostRuntime (open-source runtime + consulting)
  - Strengths: Low-level control, no vendor lock-in.
  - Redwood Differentiator: Managed serving + opinionated defaults, integrated observability and rollouts, and predictable reserved capacity options (Dedicated).
- Competitor: ModelAPI (API-first LLM providers)
  - Strengths: Simple developer UX, wide model catalog.
  - Redwood Differentiator: Cost-aware controls (batching, quantization recommendations), enterprise SLAs, and cross-environment parity (hosted -> private).

Quick rebuttals to common buyer objections:
- "We can self-host to save money": Self-hosting often underestimates SRE and optimization engineering cost; our Dedicated offering offloads fleet management, and our Optimize toolkit provides automated quantization and batching guidance that typically reduces total cost of ownership.
- "We’re worried about latency with managed providers": Redwood’s serving runtime and region-aware routing are designed for sub-100ms token latencies for common conversational models under SLOs; we provide latency heatmaps and per-token latency breakdowns in the Console.

AE pitch deck / talk track (8 slides):
1) Title and TL;DR (30s): Product teams ship faster with predictable cost and enterprise-grade controls.
2) Problem (60s): Latency surprises, rising token cost, and fragmented tooling across hosted/self-hosted models.
3) Redwood value prop (60s): Unified runtime + predictable economics + enterprise deployments.
4) How it works (90s): Runtime, kernel selection, batching, caching, routing policies (one diagram).
5) Deployment modes (60s): Hosted API, Dedicated reserved capacity, Private (VPC/on-prem).
6) Customer results (90s): Case study highlights and metrics.
7) Pricing & rollout options (60s): Self-serve to Dedicated contracts and migration path.
8) Next steps (30s): Pilot plan + evaluation checklist.

Demo checklist (SE):
- Show API quickstart (token generation and streaming)
- Demonstrate Console: per-route latency, token cost, model rollouts
- Run a live inference with prefix caching to show tail latency improvement
- Show Dedicated capacity UI and autoscaling policy example
- Show security tab: audit logs, KMS key binding, RBAC roles

Pricing guidance and examples (guidance only; final pricing per contract):
- Hosted (self-serve):
  - Generative text: $0.003 per 1k tokens (prompt) and $0.02 per 1k tokens (completion) — example: 100k prompt + 50k completion tokens => monthly cost = prompt(100 * $0.003) + completion(50 * $0.02) = $0.30 + $1.00 = $1.30 (demo-friendly numbers).
  - Embeddings: $0.0005 per embedding unit (example: 1M embeddings => $500).
- Dedicated (reserved capacity):
  - Commit tiers: Starter (4 GPUs), Growth (16 GPUs), Enterprise (64+ GPUs). Pricing includes a monthly platform fee + per-GPU reserved price; typical discount vs hosted list pricing is 35–60% depending on commit.
  - Example: 16xA10 reserved for $XX,XXX/mo (use contract-eng to generate exact quote).
- Add-ons: Advanced observability retention, HIPAA-compliance package, premium SLAs, on-prem packaging.
- Negotiation levers: commit length, burst capacity caps, retention window for logs, professional services for migration.

Pricing play examples for AE:
1) Low-touch pilot: 3–6 week hosted eval with free credits, success metrics focused on latency and unit cost reduction.
2) Mid-cycle conversion: Offer 3-month Dedicated pilot with temporary credits and migration assistance; guarantee a baseline throughput and a rollback plan.

Case studies (short, metrics-first):
- AcmeChat (SaaS startup) — Problem: unpredictable token cost and spikes when user growth accelerated.
  - Solution: Migrated from ModelAPI to Redwood Hosted + Optimize recommendations (quantization + KV caching).
  - Results: 42% reduction in per-token cost, 25% improvement in average response latency, enabled 2x concurrent user scale without infra changes.
  - Owner: Customer Success manager (CSM) contact: Priya Menon.
- FinBank (mid-market financial services) — Problem: Compliance requirements + need for private inference.
  - Solution: Private VPC deployment with KMS integration, audit logging, and RBAC; Dedicated model pool for peak hours.
  - Results: Met internal security checklist and reduced time-to-deploy from 12 weeks to 4 weeks using Redwood reference architecture; CPU/GPU utilization improved by 18%.
  - Owner: Solutions Engineering contact: Marco Silva.

Security FAQ for prospects (short answers + links to artifacts):
Q: Where does customer data live?
A: For Hosted, data is stored in region selected at account creation; for Dedicated and Private deployments, data remains in customer VPC or on-prem. See our data-residency page for region list.
Q: How is data encrypted?
A: TLS in transit; AES-256 encryption at rest. KMS integrations available for Dedicated/Private (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault, and HSM options).
Q: Do you support SOC 2 / ISO / HIPAA?
A: Redwood maintains SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 evidence. HIPAA support is available via a Business Associate Agreement (BAA) for Private or Dedicated deployments.
Q: What audit and access controls exist?
A: Console audit logs with per-request metadata, RBAC with granular roles, and support for SAML/SCIM SSO.
Q: How do you handle model provenance and PII?
A: We recommend prompt engineering and redaction at the application layer; Redwood provides PII detection helpers and model-card metadata in the Console.
Q: Incident response expectations and SLOs?
A: Standard SLA: 99.9% availability for Dedicated; Hosted SLA tiers available for enterprise customers. Incident response follows our oncall playbook with initial response targets of 15 minutes for Sev1. See incident-runbook for details.

Appendix A — Example Dedicated capacity config (YAML snippet):

apiVersion: inference.redwood/v1
kind: DedicatedPool
metadata:
  name: acme-growth-pool
spec:
  gpuType: a10g
  replicas: 16
  autoscaling:
    minReplicas: 12
    maxReplicas: 20
  routingPolicy:
    latencyTargetMs: "120"
    fallbackModels: ["redwood-small-v1","redwood-medium-v1"]

(Notes: this example is for demo only; actual API names may vary by release.)

Appendix B — Demo CLI snippets:
- Quick generate (curl):
  curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"model":"redwood-chat-1","input":"Summarize the following...","max_tokens":256}'

- List Dedicated pools (CLI):
  redwoodctl pools list --org acme --region us-west-2

Enablement playbook for AE (step-by-step):
1) Pre-call: Review prospect notes, check org plan (Hosted vs Dedicated potential), prepare cost example using pricing guidance.
2) Discovery call: Confirm workloads (QPS, avg tokens per request, peak concurrency), compliance constraints, and integration timeline.
3) Demo: Use demo checklist above and show Console metrics.
4) POA (proof-of-action) Pilot: Propose 4-week hosted pilot or 8-week Dedicated pilot with success criteria (latency < 150ms p50, cost reduction >= 20%).
5) Close: Finalize pricing levers and engineering kickoff.
